name: Sentry
verdict: Self-serve to build, but a public integration is visible only to your own organization until you click Publish, which sends it to Sentry for review. Criteria and timeline are undocumented; likely 2-6 weeks.
needGuide: Yes — build and test in your org, then request publication so other organizations can install.

auth.detail: Integration Platform. Internal integrations: org-only, token auto-generated on install. Public integrations: OAuth authorization-code style. After install Sentry sends a grant code and installation ID (redirect URL and installation.created webhook); exchange via POST /api/0/sentry-app-installations/{id}/authorizations/ with client ID/secret. Tokens expire after 8 hours; refresh with a client-secret-signed JWT (jwt-bearer grant, recommended) or a refresh token. Permissions are scoped to the organization.

approval.gate: A public integration starts unpublished: only the organization that created it can see or install it. To serve other organizations you click Publish, which emails integrations-platform@sentry.io for review. Review criteria and timeline are not documented in the pages read. Logo PNG 256-1024 px required.

scopes.why: Standard org-wide API permissions chosen on the integration and approved by users at install.
scopes.summary: Standard Sentry API permissions (for example project, issue and event read/write) are chosen when creating the integration and become the token's scopes; users approve them at install. Scopes are org-wide. Which scopes draw extra review is not documented.

prerequisites: Account and owner: Create it under your company's Sentry organization; you cannot grant the integration permissions beyond the creating user's own. Specific org role needed not documented (likely Manager or Owner).
Where you register: sentry.io → Settings → Developer Settings → New Public Integration (name, webhook URL, redirect URL, permissions, logo)

registerAt.path: sentry.io → Settings → Developer Settings → New Public Integration (name, webhook URL, redirect URL, permissions, logo)

steps.do: In your Sentry org go to Settings → Developer Settings and create a new public integration; set webhook URL, redirect URL, permissions and logo
Implement the redirect/setup endpoint: receive code and installation ID, exchange at /sentry-app-installations/{id}/authorizations/, store token and refresh token encrypted
Implement 8-hour token refresh using the JWT grant; handle installation.deleted webhooks
If Verify Install is on, PUT status=installed to /sentry-app-installations/{id}/
Install and test in your own org; ask a friendly second org to test after publishing
Click Publish next to the integration and answer follow-ups from integrations-platform@sentry.io

roles.team: Create it under your company's Sentry organization; you cannot grant the integration permissions beyond the creating user's own. Specific org role needed not documented (likely Manager or Owner).
roles.console: none documented (integrations belong to the organization)
roles.customer: A customer organization admin/owner installs the integration and approves the requested permissions (likely; roles not stated). Org-wide scope means issue/event access spans the whole organization.

testing: Develop as an unpublished public integration and install it in your own Sentry org, or use an internal integration for quick tests; use the external-install URL https://sentry.io/sentry-apps/<slug>/external-install/.
Sentry offers an example app (Python/TypeScript) with testing advice.

blockers.problem: Only the creating org can install until Sentry approves publication
blockers.fix: Plan the review wait before customer launches.

blockers.problem: Cannot request permissions the creator does not have
blockers.fix: Create it from an org owner/manager account.

blockers.problem: Browser use of tokens needs authorized origins listed (no wildcards)

automation.agentCan: Write the setup endpoint, JWT refresh and webhook handlers, draft listing description and permission justification, and run test API calls.
automation.humanMust: Log in (2FA) and create the integration, upload the logo, press Publish, and handle any Sentry review correspondence; a customer admin must install it.

uncertain: Review criteria, timeline and eligibility for publication, plus exact org roles for creating and installing, were not documented in fetched pages.
